lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Computing, Data & AI Check-In: Where Am I?
lesson.summary: Check what you know about algorithms, loops, decisions, data, and how AI learns so we can plan your coding and data year.
learning_objectives: Show I can read and fix simple algorithms
Show I can read and use data tables and charts
Show what I understand about how AI learns and staying safe online

blocks.markdown: This is a **check-in** to see what you already know about computing, data and AI. No computer is needed, just your brain and a pencil.

An **algorithm** is a precise list of steps. A **loop** repeats steps so you do not have to write them again: repeat 4 times (move forward, turn right) draws a square. **Debugging** means finding and fixing mistakes.

question.prompt: A robot does this 3 times: move 2 steps forward. How many steps does it move in total?

scenes.caption: A robot starts in the corner. The loop says: move forward, turn right.
Forward and turn right. That was one time round the loop.
Repeat! Forward and turn right again.
And again. Three times so far.
Repeat 4 times and the robot is back at the start, having drawn a square. One loop saved lots of writing!

blocks.markdown: Programs make choices with **if** statements: **if** it is raining, **then** take an umbrella, **else** wear sunglasses.

question.prompt: If it is raining take an umbrella, else wear sunglasses. It is sunny. What do you take?

blocks.title: Debug the sandwich
instructions: Write a 6 step algorithm for making a sandwich.
Swap with a grown-up who follows it exactly like a robot.
Find any step that was unclear and fix (debug) it.

blocks.markdown: **Data** is facts we collect. We store it in **tables** (rows and columns) and show it in **charts**. A **bar chart** makes comparing categories easy. Always check the labels and the scale.

blocks.title: A table: our favourite sports
blocks.caption: A table stores data in rows and columns.

blocks.title: A bar chart of the same data
blocks.caption: The taller the bar, the more votes. Football is the tallest.

question.prompt: A bar chart shows Cricket 8, Football 12, Swimming 5 votes. Which is most popular?

blocks.markdown: Some programs do not follow fixed rules. Instead they learn from many **examples**, called **training data**. If you show a computer thousands of cat and dog pictures, it learns to tell them apart. If the examples are unfair or missing, the AI can make **mistakes**, so people must check its answers.

question.prompt: An AI learns by looking at lots of examples.

blocks.markdown: A **strong password** is long and mixes words, numbers and symbols. Never share it. Think before you click or post, and tell a trusted adult if something feels wrong.

blocks.prompt: Why might an AI that only saw pictures of golden retrievers get confused by a poodle?
blocks.answer_markdown: Because it learned from a narrow set of examples. Good training data needs variety.

blocks.title: Copy the sequence
blocks.goal: Computers follow steps in order. Watch, then copy the order.

points: Algorithms are exact steps and loops repeat them.
If / else lets programs make decisions.
Tables and charts help us understand data.
AI learns from examples and can make mistakes.
Strong, secret passwords keep us safe.

blocks.markdown: Ready? Start the quiz. 12 questions, about 15 minutes. Do your best!

terms.meaning: A precise list of steps to solve a problem.
Steps that repeat so you do not have to write them again.
Finding and fixing mistakes in a program.
A graph that uses bars to compare amounts.
The examples an AI learns from.
A long mix of letters, numbers and symbols that is hard to guess.

items.text: Wait for it to pop up

Using that table (3, 7 and 5 cars), how many cars were counted in total?
Which chart is best for comparing how many students like each fruit?
